platformMeasurementsTakenBeforeWritingTh: fs.symlinkSync(target, link, 'junction') succeeds unprivileged here; fs.lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink() is true and fs.realpathSync.native(link) differs from path.resolve(link).

fs.rmSync(link, { recursive: true, force: true }) on a junction removes the link ONLY - the junction target's file survived. So 'delete the junction recursively' is not observable through that call, and the M3 mutant must resolve the link first (fs.rmSync(fs.realpathSync.native(link), { recursive: true, force: true }) DID delete the target's contents in the same probe).
fs.unlinkSync(junction) succeeds on this platform and the target survives, so the implementation's EPERM fallback to fs.rmdirSync is defensive rather than exercised here.
fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }) reports a junction entry with isSymbolicLink() === true, so the walk can skip links without following them.

redB.whyThisShapeOfFixture: path.relative fails to produce a relative path in exactly two shapes: the two sides share no root (different drives - Windows only) or they are the SAME path. Only the second has a POSIX equivalent, so the case points repoRoot at the preserved directory itself. A cross-drive fixture would pass on this machine and never run the assertion on Linux CI.

platformMeasurementsForTheFix.symlinkPrivilege: fs.symlinkSync(target, link, 'dir') and (..., 'file') both fail EPERM on this machine, so a real POSIX-shaped symlink could not be created here and the symlink half of the analysis is measured by proxy plus git's documented semantics, labelled below.
measured: In a scratch repository ignoring 'slashed/' and 'bare', a NON-DIRECTORY entry named slashed is NOT ignored (git check-ignore exit 1, git status --porcelain prints '?? slashed') while a non-directory entry named bare IS ignored (exit 0, '.gitignore:2:bare	bare'). This is the trailing-slash rule measured directly: a slash-terminated pattern matches directories only.

In the pin's own fixture shape (a junction planted in the worktree), '.gitignore' without a node_modules entry gives git status --porcelain '?? node_modules/' and check-ignore exit 1; with 'node_modules/' it gives empty status and check-ignore exit 0 matching '.gitignore:1:node_modules/'; with bare 'node_modules' it gives empty status and check-ignore exit 0 matching '.gitignore:1:node_modules'. So the bare spelling matches a Windows junction too - it loses nothing on this platform and gains the POSIX symlink.

LABELLED AS PROXY, NOT DIRECT: the symlink case itself was not executed here. git stores a symlink as a blob and presents it to the exclude machinery as a non-directory, the same class as the regular file measured above; combined with the documented trailing-slash rule, that is why 'node_modules/' leaves a POSIX symlink untracked. The direct evidence for the symlink is the CI failure itself.
